title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, and server timeouts
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Add streaming lifecycle controls: client-initiated cancel, server-side timeouts, robust disconnect handling, and optional resume semantics for reconnects. Backwards-compatible API surface; SDKs updated.
description:
Motivation: We observed several production incidents where long-lived streaming responses (chat/generation + tool calls) were not cleaned up correctly after client disconnects or cancellations, leading to leaked server work and stuck KV cache entries. This PR adds explicit lifecycle controls for streaming RPCs: client-initiated cancel semantics, improved disconnect handling on transport loss, optional reconnect/resume handshake, and server-side idle/processing timeouts.

Design summary: Implement a lifecycle manager in the streaming runtime that tracks stream state (open, cancelled, disconnected, resumed, finished). Expose lifecycle control messages in the OpenAI-compatible streaming adapter and SDKs so clients can send cancel frames or reconnect with resume tokens. On server side, introduce configurable timeouts: idle_timeout (no client activity), processing_timeout (per-request processing limit), and resume_expiry (how long resume tokens remain valid). The manager guarantees cleanup of KV cache and background work when streams are cancelled or expire.

Implementation details: - runtime/stream_manager.py: new StreamLifecycleManager that maintains in-memory stream registry, resume tokens, and finalizer hooks. - openai_compat/streaming_adapter.py: supports new control frames: "cancel", "resume_request", and "resume_response" while preserving existing text/event-stream behavior. - sdk-python/redwood/streaming.py and sdk-typescript/src/streaming.ts: added client APIs cancel_stream(handle) and resume_stream(handle, token) plus docs/examples. - grpc/proto changes: streaming.proto extended with optional control messages (backwards-compatible: unknown control messages are ignored by older clients). - gateway timeouts: deploy/gateway/timeouts.yaml adds default idle_timeout: 30s and processing_timeout: 120s. - tests: tests/test_streaming_lifecycle.py covers disconnects, resume happy-path, expired resume tokens, and server timeouts.

Compatibility and safety: Behavior is backwards-compatible for clients that continue to use text/event-stream without control frames; servers will still close streams normally on EOF. New resume feature is opt-in and requires the client to request a resume token on stream start. Resume tokens are opaque, single-use, and TTL-bound.

Checklist: - [x] StreamLifecycleManager core logic + registry - [x] OpenAI-compatible control frames implemented - [x] SDK client cancel/resume APIs added with examples - [x] Gateway defaults and flags for operators - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Updated docs (console + SDK quickstarts)

Testing and validation: Ran integration suite against local gateway and a canary cluster. Simulated flaky networks to verify cleanup on disconnect and observed no KV cache leaks after cancel/timeout. Load tests: no measurable regression in steady-state throughput; small increase in memory transient due to registry entries (cleaned within TTL).

Related work: ENG-4123 (streaming reliability epic), ENG-4187 (resume semantics design doc).

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on race conditions in StreamLifecycleManager.finalize_stream and the correctness of resume token single-use enforcement. Also review the gateway timeout defaults and whether they should be shorter for low-latency tiers.
